overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation because the June 8 minutes request was sent only to the town's Records Access Officer, not to the Board, so it fell under the Public Records Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to respond within 10 days to his June 8 emailed request to inspect all open and executive session minutes from 2019.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the request for meeting minutes was not a request that fell under the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, § 22(c), (g)(2), and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.
